quote: a 0 leaves it off, and the supply holds the output at 1
problem: The reader is told the output is held at 1 by 'the supply' and also connected to 0 volts when the transistor is on. Nothing says why 0 V wins while the supply is still attached, or how the supply is joined to the output. It also does not square with the AND/OR half of the same paragraph, where conducting means 1, not 0.
fix: say the supply reaches the output through a resistance (like Fig 1.4's lamp), so the transistor's direct path to 0 V pulls the output down
reason: Checked ch2-gates-p2 and Fig 1.4. Fig 1.4 draws a lamp, not a pull-up, and nothing says how the supply reaches the output. The sentence puts the output at 0 V (transistor on) and at 1 (supply) with no word on which wins, so an attentive reader asks why there is no short circuit. The AND/OR half is not a contradiction, since the paragraph marks NOT as a separate case. The gap is only that the supply and the transistor are never shown to be alternatives.
judge_fix: Replace the NOT sentence with: "For NOT, two transistors take turns: a 1 at the input switches on one that connects the output to 0 volts and switches the other off, cutting the output from the supply; a 0 does the reverse, and the supply holds the output at 1." This matches how modern chips work and avoids a resistor model. The shorter option is "...the supply, joined to the output through a resistor, holds it at 1, and an on transistor's direct path to 0 volts overpowers it."

quote: by twenty-six with no university degree, and by thirty-two was publishing original mathematics
problem: Both ages are too late, so the reader comes away with the wrong timeline. Boole opened his own school in Lincoln in 1834, at 19. His first paper appeared in the Cambridge Mathematical Journal in February 1840, at 24, and the Royal Society gave him its Royal Medal in 1844, at 28, for 'On a General Method in Analysis'. 'By thirty-two' points at 1847, so it reads as though The Mathematical Analysis of Logic was where his mathematics began.
fix: Replace the sentence with: "Taught Latin by a local bookseller, he taught himself Greek, French and German, opened his own school at nineteen with no university degree, and at twenty-four was publishing original mathematics." Sources: mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Boole/ (school in 1834 'although he was only 19'; Royal Medal November 1844); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Boole (first paper February 1840; own school at 19).
reason: Verified at MacTutor: he opened his own school in Lincoln in 1834 'although he was only 19', and regular publishing in the Cambridge Mathematical Journal began about 1840 (age 24-25); Royal Medal Nov 1844 (age 28). 'By twenty-six' and 'by thirty-two' are true only as loose upper bounds, and they read as milestones. 'By thirty-two' lands on 1847, the year of the book, so it suggests his mathematics began there. Severity M.
judge_fix: Replace the sentence with: "Taught Latin by a local bookseller, he taught himself Greek, French and German, opened his own school at nineteen with no university degree, and by twenty-five was publishing original mathematics." Use 'by twenty-five' rather than 'at twenty-four': MacTutor gives only 'after 1840' for his first paper, and the paper dates to 1840-41, so 'by twenty-five' holds either way. Sources: mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Boole/ (school 1834 aged 19; Latin from a local bookseller; Royal Medal Nov 1844).

quote: in Python, JavaScript, C, Java and Rust alike
problem: C computes the same double, but it does not show 0.30000000000000004 by default. printf("%f") prints 0.300000 and %g prints 0.3. You only see the long form if you ask for 17 digits. Python, JavaScript, Java and Rust print it unprompted. A reader who tries it in C will see 0.3.
fix: "in Python, JavaScript, Java and Rust alike" (drop C), or "... Java and Rust alike, and in C when asked for 17 digits".
reason: The C double is the same, but C does not print the long form by default: printf("%f") gives 0.300000 and %g gives 0.3. A reader who tries it in C sees 0.3 and doubts the book. Python, JavaScript, Java and Rust all print the shortest round-trip string, 0.30000000000000004. The claim that follows (they agree because they all use the processor's binary doubles) survives without C. Severity L.
judge_fix: "...in Python, JavaScript, Java and Rust alike." Leave the rest of the paragraph unchanged.

judge_fix: The 1991 Patriot missile failure during the Gulf War, in which a Scud killed 28 American soldiers, came from the same endless 0.1. Relabel that wire '¬B' and the AND's output wire 'A · ¬B', and re-route the output wire from x 226 to the OR as is. With A = 1, B = 0 the top AND gives 1, so change the final output label from '0' to '1'.
